lines: Multi-agent wave (Analyst → Architect → QA → Dev ↔ Reviewer)

card.summary: Multi-agent feature wave. Analyst → Architect → QA → Dev with Reviewer gate between Dev and QA. Three approval gates, orchestrator-run interviews (subagents can't reach the user), tier-specialized Devs, suspicious-change tracking, reviewer_verdicts[] trail. Agents write only wave-state.json; every HTML artifact is rendered from it deterministically, so the two can't drift. --autonomous mode auto-approves all gates for unattended runs (never commits). Personas live in .claude/agents/.
card.paragraph: Drives a multi-agent feature wave. Spawns a worktree, builds a codebase-map.md index once so no agent has to re-walk the repo, interviews the user up front (orchestrator-run — agents that hit a blocking ambiguity hand back an open_questions[] block instead of asking directly), then runs Analyst → Architect → QA in sequence (each behind a user gate unless --autonomous), then dispatches tier-specialized Dev agents under QA control until all tests are green. Each agent gets a brief — the slice of state its role needs — rather than the previous agent's rendered HTML.
use_when: Feature decomposes into multiple tasks across tiers
You want failing tests written before any code
You want a written architecture decision, not freeform
dontuse_when: Refactor with no behavior change (no failing test)

extras.title: Artifacts produced
rows: Canonical state and the only file agents write — features, tasks, suspicious[], escalations[], gates[]
Index of components, routes, services, tests and doc headings — built once per wave
Per-role slices of state handed to each agent at spawn
Gate 2 — freezes out-of-scope; §3 Revisions derived from escalations[]
End-of-wave summary (gates, reviewer verdicts, suspicious changes)

extras.title: Iteration caps
items: Soft cap 3 / task — Architect re-engages, may append Revision N to architecture-verse.
Hard cap 5 / task — wave halts, handoff.md written.
Suspicious-changes 3 / task — auto-halt task (scope-drift, test-file touch, mock-of-SUT, build-break).
Autonomous never bypasses reviewer halt verdicts, iteration caps, destructive ops, or commit/PR steps.

extras.title: Deterministic artifacts
items: Agents write JSON, never HTML. The bundled stx-feature render produces every artifact from wave-state.json, so the HTML cannot say something the state does not.
Derived, not stored: Architect Revisions come from escalations[]; reviewer-rejection counts, iteration totals and agent tallies are computed at render time.
Validation is a halt condition. stx-feature validate rejects malformed state by field path and the renderer writes nothing.
Never hand-edit a rendered artifact — change the state and re-render. Rendering is idempotent.
